verdict_template.unassured: Nothing is visibly wrong, but {unassured} of {total} of the things holding this look together are checked by eye alone.
verdict_template.ok: The look is holding, and what checks it runs on every page load.

goals.statement: Every picture and sound in the game has a written record of where it came from.
goals.statement_short: a sound in the game has no record of where it came from
goals.why_it_matters: CREDITS.md's own rule is that nothing ships without verified terms. An asset with no line is the release-blocking kind of unknown, and it is invisible until somebody looks.

measure.unit: shipped file with no record of where it came from
measure.unit_plural: shipped files with no record of where they came from

path_to_green.narrative: Write the missing ledger lines — where each file came from, its terms, and what it cost.

action.label: Put it on Ingrid's list
action.ask: A shipped sound has no provenance line. Trace it and write the entry, or recommend dropping it — the standing policy is to drop a restrictively-licensed or unprovenanced asset rather than work around its terms.
action.first_action: Trace the file through git history to the commit that added it, then write or recommend.
action.title: Trace the unledgered sound and write its entry

goals.statement: Every sound in the repo is one the build actually plays.
goals.statement_short: a sound file ships that the build never loads
goals.why_it_matters: A sound nobody loads is either a forgotten cut or a wiring bug, and from the outside those look identical.

path_to_green.narrative: Either wire it up or delete it. The sound board below marks which files the build never loads.

action.label: Put it on Dmitri's list
action.ask: A sound file ships that systems/audio_manager.gd never loads. From outside, a forgotten cut and a wiring bug look identical — work out which this is, then either wire it up or delete it and say why in the commit.
action.first_action: Compare assets/audio/sfx against the preloads in systems/audio_manager.gd, then listen to the orphan and decide.
action.title: Wire up the orphaned sound or delete it

goals.statement: The colours the style guide names are still the colours in the build.
goals.statement_short: colours the style guide names have vanished from the build
goals.why_it_matters: Drift is invisible one sprite at a time. A named colour disappearing is the first measurable sign the guide and the game have parted company.

path_to_green.narrative: The look session decides whether the missing names come back into the art or come out of the guide. Both are fine; the split is not.

ceo_blocker.consequence: The style guide stays a draft nobody is bound by, and every new sprite is a fresh taste call.

goals.statement: The art direction is signed, so a new sprite has a rule to follow rather than a taste to guess.
goals.statement_short: the art direction is still a draft nobody is bound by

measure.reason: Whether a style guide is signed is a judgment you make in a room, not a string in a file. Nothing here can measure it, and a checkbox in the document would only measure whether somebody ticked a checkbox.
measure.would_need: Your yes in a look session, recorded as a ruling — then this row becomes an attestation with a date rather than a blank.

path_to_green.narrative: One look session. You asked for it before signing, and it has not been booked.

ceo_blocker.consequence: Every sprite generated before the signing is a guess that may have to be redone.

goals.statement: When you hand-edit a sprite in HQ, you are editing the whole sheet.
goals.statement_short: the sprite editor silently edits part of a sheet, not all of it
goals.why_it_matters: The editor opens the entity catalog's preview frames, not the sheet — Chicken lists four of its eight cells, the farmer four of sixteen. A hand edit therefore touches a quarter of a sheet without saying so.

measure.reason: No check compares the frames the editor opens against the cells the sheet holds; the defect is known from reading the code, not from a measurement.
measure.would_need: A check that every sheet's cell count equals the frame count the editor opens for it — cheap, and it would have caught this.

path_to_green.narrative: The editor should open every cell of a sheet, with the animating frames only highlighted. Filed against the design-technology seat.

action.label: Put it on Rin's list
action.ask: HQ's sprite editor opens the entity catalogue's preview frame list rather than the sheet — Chicken lists four of its eight cells, the farmer four of sixteen — so a hand edit silently touches part of a sheet without saying so. The editor should open every cell of a sheet, with the animating frames only highlighted as what animates.
action.first_action: Read hq/static/sprite.js and hq/data/entities.json, and confirm the frame-count mismatch on Chicken and Farmer before changing anything.
action.title: Make the sprite editor open the whole sheet
